conclusions: SO_CONNECT_TIME is useful coarse negative admission evidence without listener rotation or connection maps, but the cited contract does not prove a finite tight upper bound for true ESTABLISHED age; neither s+1 seconds nor0meansfresh is documented.

A completion-time age query may prevent granting an obviously aged connection another full post+5 interval; it cannot retroactively close a backlog connection before a five-second deadline already exceeded while Net was unscheduled.
TCP_ESTATS_SYN_OPTS_ROS_v0 contains no time. SIO_TCP_INFO.ConnectionTimeMs is Windows10version1703+ and cannot satisfy the Win7 baseline.

Pre-new-local-connect to causally corresponding remote-close observation can be a conservative longer per-sample interval without cross-machine clock alignment. It is conditional on actual remote connection/EOF provenance and cannot turn all current forwardObservation fields into strict transport proof automatically.

supportedFacts.unit: seconds since connected, per document; integer output
supportedFacts.minimumAvailability: Win7/10 explicitly listed; current SDK retains API. Win11 uses the same supported Winsock API family, exact provider success still must be checked; no claim of Win7/10/11 runtime execution here.
supportedFacts.unconnected: AcceptEx/ConnectEx pages describe returned optval0xFFFFFFFF; generic getsockopt prose says SOCKET_ERROR. Therefore distinguish API return code from DWORD sentinel instead of reading optval on error.
supportedFacts.integerRange: DWORD representable0..4294967295;0xFFFFFFFF is reserved here as unconnected. Documentation does not specify large-age saturation/wrap semantics.

soConnectTime.safetyConsequence: Do not compute a strict deadline as dequeueNow+(5-s)seconds or5-(s+1)seconds and label it proven. A finite provider measurement may characterize observed behavior only, not establish a general documented error bound.
boundedIntegrationCandidate: Query the exact bare-owned accepted socket after actual AcceptEx completion and SO_UPDATE_ACCEPT_CONTEXT, before SSPI/ownership transfer; no lookup table, no worker/native thread, no extra socket/Frame.

Validate getsockopt return0 and returned optlen==sizeof(DWORD); treat error, sentinel or unsupported provider as unavailable age, never fresh age0. A chosen fail-closed rejection policy must be explicit and tested; no reopen/rotation/reuseaddr.

Coarse values indicating aged connection may justify immediate negative discard, with reported units and uncertainty; successful age reading must never extend the already captured post-derived header deadline.

Recheck original header alarm/deadline after the query and immediately before handoff. Once complete valid Head entered the original120-second request stage, do not let an age>=5 observation kill legitimate admitted body/response.
If close fails or cancellation/IOCP return is outstanding, keep the exact existing bare owner and prohibit replacement; metadata query is not physical close/IO completion proof.

synOpts.collection: SynOpts exempt from prior collection enabling. Other groups generally require enable; do not enable stats/UAC merely to search for nonexistent time.

estatsAndAlternatives.otherGroups: Data counters, RTT and cumulative congestion-limited durations describe transfer behavior, not a reliable per-link ESTABLISHED timestamp. Row tuple lookup additionally faces snapshot/tuple reuse races and system table allocation; do not introduce an unbounded connection map as a workaround.
estatsAndAlternatives.ownerModuleTimestamp: MIB_TCPROW_OWNER_MODULE.liCreateTimestamp is documented context-bind FILETIME, not ESTABLISHED. It is wall-clock metadata and not a substitute for a monotonic deadline origin.
estatsAndAlternatives.newWindowsInfo: TCP_INFO_v0.ConnectionTimeMs is a millisecond lifetime field requiring Win10version1703+; even then cited docs provide no strict quantization/refresh bound. A runtime-probed optional diagnostic does not become Win7 coverage or hard real-time proof.

currentSourceFindings.fact: post_bare_accept still captures deadline after AcceptEx success/IO_PENDING. Dequeue latency and an already-established backlog predecessor can make this origin later than remote ESTABLISHED.
header_close_alarm subtracts HEADER_CLOSE_RESERVE from the existing hard deadline. This is scheduling/close margin, not a kernel connection birth timestamp or backlog-age correction.

existingStartSites.observation: Client.request uses monotonic_ns before constructing/sending a fresh local connection; EOF occurs before finally local close and final elapsed capture.
PendingReceipt starts before its fresh local TCP connect; final elapsed includes intentionally held body and is not an incomplete-Head deadline test.
capacity reject start is pre-local-connect, but raw SSLEOF/RST alone may also arise from forwarding failure, so provenance matters.
exercise_batch uses one shared pre-barrier start earlier than every new local connect; it is a looser lower origin, not per-connection serverEST. Closing in finally precedes final time capture.
-L master listener is established before individual sockets; successful mux forward acknowledgement proves local forward listener, not a particular remote TCP connection.

causalArgument.classification: Inference from actual new OpenSSH-L connection semantics and trusted peer correlation; not an OS timing API fact
causalArgument.chain: t0(client before creating new local socket) <= tWindowsEST(for that new remote connection) <= tRemoteEOF(or that server TLS close_notify emission) <= tObservedPeerEvent(client read result) <= tAfterLocalClose(finally timer)
causalArgument.inequality: For the same causal remote connection and endpoint event: tObservedPeerEvent-tWindowsEST <= tObservedPeerEvent-t0 <= tAfterLocalClose-t0. No wall-clock alignment is needed because the containing interval is measured entirely by one local monotonic clock.
causalArgument.pass: If the properly correlated containing interval<=5000000000ns, it gives a conservative sampled upper interval for the contained EST-to-observed-peer-event duration, including SSH/network/client scheduling overhead.
causalArgument.failure: If the containing interval>5000000000ns, retain conservative observationFAIL/NOT_PROVEN, but do not infer server uniquely violated its internal closure deadline; overhead may be outside the server. No claim about arbitrary scheduling follows from any finite PASS.

requiredConditions: t0 must precede the actual local socket connect that causes a new remote direct-tcpip connection; it cannot be handshake complete, local connect return, accepted_at or reused HTTP keepalive/pooled tunnel destination.
The same local socket must causally lead to this exact owned Windows listener. An already open SSH master is acceptable; a preconnected remote destination pool is not.

Positive evidence must exclude SSH channel-open/refused/forward teardown/client timeout/local cancel/process stop as the source of EOF. Completed TLS1.2 handshake against the exact owned certificate establishes service reachability for partial-HTTP tests; no-TLS-data tests need separate bounded remote attribution.

Observe and record the recv EOF/RST/TLS result timestamp before actively closing the local socket; record localClose separately. Existing later finally elapsed is only a looser bound and never converts an exception/no-EOF into peer closure.

TLS recv returningempty with suppress_ragged_eofs=False proves close_notify, not Windows TCP FIN or socket/IOCP retirement. Raw recv0 proves local forwarded-stream EOF; corresponding remote TCP provenance still must be established. Keep these distinct.
A complete HTTPHead ends the first-head gate. Ordinary successful API response duration, body-held PendingReceipt and late application responses cannot test incomplete-Head closure.

Preserve exact per-connection sample/raw timestamps plus the original5000000000 threshold. Do not round milliseconds, omit outliers, renew client/native budget, or reinterpret proxy delay as exact kernel time.
forwardedTiming.currentEvidenceVerdict: Existing forwardObservationNanos starts early enough for a causal upper interval in successfully reached-service cases, but current generic flags remain NOT_VALIDATED: no dedicated strict incomplete-Head assertion/end timestamp/provenance ledger for all negative paths. Do not retroactively promote old reports.

primarySources.supports: SO_CONNECT_TIME is get-only DWORD connected seconds; Win7/10 support table. No rounding/update/overflow bound stated.
Return0 vs SOCKET_ERROR, optlen bytes, unsupported option error; unconnected discussion differs from AcceptEx sentinel description.
ReceiveDataLength0 completes on arriving connection; pending-accept connected seconds and 0xFFFFFFFF unconnected sentinel; update accept context; actual cancellation completion still matters.
Connected-seconds query while pending and unconnected optval0xFFFFFFFF.
Microsoft SDK defines SO_CONNECT_TIME0x700C and SO_UPDATE_ACCEPT_CONTEXT0x700B; no age accuracy guarantee.
Vista+ IPv4 tuple-based statistics; SynOpts needs no prior collection enable, other groups generally do; no per-socket establishment-time contract.
Only ActiveOpen/MssRcvd/MssSent fields, immutable after SYN exchange. No timestamp.
Microsoft SDK confirms SynOpts three fields and separate counter/RTT/cumulative-duration groups; no connection creation timestamp in SynOpts/Data structures.
Data transfer counters/sequence state, not connection establishment time.
ConnectionTimeMs lifetime in milliseconds; minimum Windows10version1703, so not a Win7 fallback.
WSAIoctl socket statistics versioned operation; v0/v1 output, not a common Win7 API.
liCreateTimestamp is FILETIME of context bind creating TCP link, not a documented ESTABLISHED transition timestamp.
